units.notes: Evergy's 2025 plan documents gave 338 MW for the gas conversion. In May 2026 Evergy told the Lawrence Journal-World the conversion is scrapped indefinitely, so the unit stays shelved and gets no start year. No turbine or boiler maker is named and no air permit for the conversion was found in the Kansas permit index.

Owner(s).note: Evergy's 2024 annual report lists Lawrence Energy Center units 4 and 5 with all 485 MW in the Evergy Kansas Central column and none for the other Evergy companies. So Kansas Central holds the whole plant. The report does not use the word percent for this plant.

Latitude.note: A satellite picture of GEM's point shows the plant site. It shows the boiler house, a coal pile, a rail spur, a switchyard and cooling ponds beside the Kansas River. The imagery date is unknown. The EIA-860M table for August 2026 places the plant at 39.0072, -95.26917, about 150 meters south of GEM's point. Both fall on the same site.

Longitude.note: Same check as latitude. GEM's point is on the plant. The EIA-860M table gives -95.26917, about 150 meters away.

Location accuracy.note: The picture shows the plant footprint under the crosshair, so exact stays correct.

qa.recommendation: Keep shelved. GEM already shows shelved. The Lawrence Journal-World article at https://www2.ljworld.com/news/general-news/2026/may/15/evergy-drops-plans-to-end-coal-burning-at-lawrence-energy-center-by-2028-not-clear-when-coal-burning-may-stop/ says Evergy confirmed the conversion is scrapped indefinitely and quotes Evergy's December 2025 letter to the state: "Evergy has chosen to maintain the coal combustion option." The status, Latest Activity and Status Detail edits for this unit use that article. The start year stays blank because shelved units never get one.
qa.note: I read the Lawrence Journal-World article of May 15, 2026 and Evergy's June 2026 plan update slides. I also searched for the full 2026 Kansas Central plan, the Kansas Corporation Commission docket, Evergy news releases and 2026 coverage from the Kansas Reflector, KCUR and the Topeka Capital-Journal, and found nothing more. I could not read Evergy's December 2025 letter to the Kansas Department of Health and Environment, so its quote comes only through the newspaper.
